text:
ajay: Heads-up — CA tried to scale down the gpu-pool in us-west-2 at ~11:42 but failed. Lots of "pods not evictable due to PDB" in the logs. Any quick wins?

sre-bot: [alert] cluster-autoscaler: scale-down blocked: 3 non-evictable pods found on candidate node ip-10-0-4-22 (reason: pdb)

maria: Can you paste the CA log snippet and a `kubectl get pdb -A`? I want to see which PDBs are blocking.

ajay: Sure — log excerpt below: 
```
I0318 11:42:12 scale_down.go:419] considering node ip-10-0-4-22 for removal
I0318 11:42:12 scale_down.go:530] node has 4 pods, 3 non-evictable:
  - ns:ml-jobs pod:trainer-abc (pdb: ml-trainer-pdb minAvailable=1)
  - ns:infra pod:gpu-preemptible-daemon (daemonset)
  - ns:batch pod:gpu-batch-runner (pdb: batch-runner-pdb minAvailable=1)
scale-down: aborting removal: pods with PDBs prevent eviction
```

And PDBs: 
```
$ kubectl get pdb -A
NAMESPACE      NAME                 MIN-AVAILABLE   MAX-UNAVAILABLE   ALLOWED-DISRUPTIONS   AGE
ml-jobs        ml-trainer-pdb       1               0                 0                     14d
batch          batch-runner-pdb     1               0                 0                     3d
stateful-prod  sfs-pdb              2               0                 0                     90d
```

ben: Ok, classic. CA won't remove a node if PDBs say you must keep X replicas. Two directions: 1) make some pods evictable (lower priority / mark safe-to-evict), or 2) temporarily relax PDBs via automation during scale events. Both have tradeoffs.

keren: For (1) I think we can convert non-critical trainer replicas to a low-priority PriorityClass so they can be preempted and allow scale-down. Suggestion: add a PriorityClass `gpu-ephemeral` with `value: 100` and patch deployments/statefulsets that are ok to lose.

maria: How exactly does CA decide evictable? Quick checklist: 
 - Pod is not a mirror pod or DaemonSet
 - Pod doesn't have `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"`
 - PDB allows eviction (i.e., allowed disruptions > 0)
 - Pod is not using local-storage without --delete-local-data

ben: Right. Two practical ops: 
1) For batch/ephemeral jobs set annotation `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "true"` and `priorityClassName: gpu-ephemeral`. That makes CA willing to evict if PDB isn't blocking.
2) For PDBs that are overly strict (minAvailable >=1 for >1 replica sets) we can implement a controller to toggle `minAvailable` during controlled scale-down windows.

ajay: We should avoid manual PDB edits during production. Prefer the priority-class route + small controller to bump `allowedDisruptions` temporarily. Who can draft the patch?

keren: I'll open a tiny k8s Job that patches deployments matching `app=trainer` to add `priorityClassName: gpu-ephemeral` and annotation `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "true"`. Patch example: 
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: trainer
  namespace: ml-jobs
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "true"
    spec:
      priorityClassName: gpu-ephemeral
```

maria: Also we should add a small read-only probe in CA runbook: `./tools/ca-checker.sh --node ip-10-0-4-22` that lists blocking PDBs/pods and suggests patch commands. That will speed triage.

ben: Note: DaemonSet (gpu-preemptible-daemon) won't be evicted — DSs are fine, CA ignores them but they reduce node capacity. Consider converting some node-local exporters to run on a different pool or use tolerations so they don't live on GPU nodes.

ajay: Action items: 
 - keren: create `PriorityClass` yaml + runbook snippet to patch non-critical apps (ETA EOD)
 - maria: add CA-checker script to infra/tools and a Grafana panel showing number of pdb-blocked scale-downs (ETA tomorrow)
 - ben: evaluate moving infra daemonsets off gpu nodes (small migration plan)

keren: Quick follow-up — small safety note: do NOT set `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "true"` for stateful-prod or sfs pods. Only for jobs and stateless trainers.

maria: I'll also add a periodic job that validates PDBs for pools tagged `autoscale:true` and alerts when minAvailable >1 for replica sets with <N replicas (N depends on pool).

ajay: Cool. For immediate relief I manually scaled down one replica set in ml-jobs to 0 replicas, CA retried and succeeded removing one node. Will follow up with the infra PR. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: [note] automated scale event succeeded at 11:58 after manual replica adjustment.

ben: Thanks all. Let's keep the changes scoped (priorityclass + safe-to-evict for ephemeral only). We should validate end-to-end in staging before rolling to prod.

keren: I'll post the PR link here when ready.
